## Architecture and acceptance boundaries

Keep detached numeric recipes for now. A future shared-buffer/Geometry design could avoid copying and repeated creation/upload, but would change the tested lifetime boundary. Before authorizing it, require measured dominant cost and an explicit scene-local owner with leases: fresh meshes/state/transforms/gauges; immutable shared attributes/indices with enforced copy-on-write or rejection of mutation; disposal only after both cache ownership and live references end; safe eviction/admission fallback; one deterministic context-rebuild owner and stale-generation cancellation. Count retained CPU arrays, active/pinned references and GPU allocations separately under explicit limits. The current32 MiB number excludes JS object and driver overhead and cannot silently cover newly resident GPU buffers. Test simultaneous IDs, mutation isolation, same-ID hull replacement, unload/re-entry, scene teardown and real context restore/deliberate resume. Materials remain scene-owned; no all-region scene retention. None of that redesign is authorized by this report.

Authored pre-baking could address expensive first construction, but numeric cache hits already skip primitive creation. Pre-baking alone still needs live handles, buffer submission and labels on a warm return. Its download/decode/first-use cost needs separate accounting; there is no evidence it fixes these current tails. Similarly, scheduling work across callbacks would need an explicit visibility/readiness/input contract and whole-transition validation, not a smaller counter obtained by moving the stall.

For root and reviewers, keep **three distinct records**: (1) unchanged shared-host wall trials, still failed with all historical/current misses; (2) attributed application work and lifecycle/output preservation; (3) representative dedicated-GPU pacing and human experience, still unverified. Absolute wall maxima on a contended emulated host include delays the application cannot bound, but current evidence does not establish that every miss is such a delay. Neither medians nor CPU-time subtraction convert these failed trials to passes. Any evidence-based disposition must be explicit in root's contract/review record and considered by both fresh complete-batch reviewers; it cannot retroactively erase failures or use the hardware exception as a waiver.

Full-game development needs a dependable return/replacement architecture and an honest target-hardware measurement path, not endless small optimizations under uncontrolled scheduling. Cold loading, larger-region/fleet scale, continuous motion/input feel, human learning/enjoyment/duration and audible mix remain open. The present advisory changes no acceptance status.
